tickets.title: Prepare mortgage liquidity source analysis
tickets.text: Prepare a written source-order plan comparing bank cash, short-term bond holdings, taxable brokerage sales, and vested employer shares to fund the remaining down payment for the Portland townhouse purchase while preserving Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk’s stated $80,000 post-closing emergency reserve target. Use their $214,000 and $138,000 salaries, $9,600 monthly spending, $286,000 brokerage account, $118,000 vested shares, and $172,000 current cash.
tickets.evidence: Julian asked for a mortgage liquidity source analysis comparing bank cash, short-term bond holdings, taxable brokerage sales, and vested employer shares to fund the remaining down payment while preserving the stated reserve target; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-08.

tickets.title: Collect underwriting asset documentation
tickets.text: Upload the most recent Teacup Comet Bank statement and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statement to the lender’s portal to document the earnest money withdrawal source account. The underwriter is asking for this documentation tying the $25,000 deposit to the source account.
tickets.evidence: the lender’s portal shows the most recent Teacup Comet Bank statement and Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage statement have not been uploaded, and the underwriter is asking for documentation tying the earnest money withdrawal to the source account; this remains needed by 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Review cash-flow effect of rate-lock alternatives
tickets.text: Review the cash-flow effect of the updated loan terms’ rate-lock choice and financing contingency timeline before Julian responds. The mortgage contact sent updated terms with a rate-lock choice and financing contingency timeline.
tickets.evidence: The mortgage contact sent updated loan terms with a rate-lock choice and financing contingency timeline, and Julian wants the cash-flow effect of the lock alternatives reviewed before he responds; the agreed review is due 2025-10-10.

tickets.title: Resolve student loan payment discrepancy
tickets.text: Resolve the $230 per month difference between the mortgage application’s $640 monthly student loan payment for Iris and the $410 income-driven payment shown on her current servicer statement. Reconcile the debt-to-income calculation for underwriting.
tickets.evidence: the mortgage application lists Iris’s student loan payment as $640 per month, while the current servicer statement provided by Iris shows a $410 income-driven payment, creating a different debt-to-income calculation for underwriting; resolution remains needed by 2025-10-07.

tickets.title: Update brokerage aggregation feed
tickets.text: Update the Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal to reflect the current joint brokerage balance and short-term bond positions, so the liquidity worksheet accurately shows available cash for closing.
tickets.evidence: The Velvet Acorn Custody aggregation feed in the planning portal is showing a stale joint brokerage balance, so the liquidity worksheet is not reflecting the current cash and short-term bond positions available for closing; the agreed follow-up is due 2025-10-06.

tickets.title: Coordinate new-home insurance and liability
tickets.text: Coordinate new-home insurance and liability coverage for the Portland townhouse purchase. The couple currently has only renters coverage; new-home insurance and updated liability protection are needed.
tickets.evidence: The townhouse purchase changes the household’s property and liability exposure, and the couple has only renters coverage in place through their current policy set; the agreed new-home insurance and liability coordination is due 2025-10-15.

tickets.title: Review tax-lot selection for down-payment cash
tickets.text: Review the taxable ETF positions in Julian and Iris Nettlewhisk’s Velvet Acorn Custody brokerage account to identify which holdings have short-term gain lots versus lower-gain long-term lots, determining the most suitable assets for brokerage-based down-payment cash.
tickets.evidence: Lena noted that several taxable ETF positions have both short-term gain lots and lower-gain long-term lots, affecting which holdings may be most suitable if brokerage assets are used for closing cash; the agreed tax-lot review is due 2025-10-09.
